content: {"rule": "K-C", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge text rules on D5 vs C5 by considering the chapter-bound witnesses and the Matthew 1:23 application, so it is the kind of chain/witness collision the rule governs.", "verdict": "CLEAN", "quote": "D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- the sign's chapter bounds (Isaiah 7:16; 8:3-4; 8:8) are real, but C5's own narrowing concedes Matthew 1:23's application stands, and the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways (Joel 1:8); answered in [CR2] section G and [CR3] LINK 5.", "rule_words": "When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.", "room": "weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse: (1) strict reading forbids even mentioning isolated verses or words in the ruling; (2) contextual reading forbids only deciding by the retired stating-verse test, while allowing a summary that acknowledges individual evidence.", "why": "The judge text labels the link underdetermined after weighing the chapter bounds against the Matthew 1:23 application and the lexical point; it does not reject the link because no single verse states the contrary in its own words."}
